data.narrative:
GITAI, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $129M+ to date, was valued using two triangulation methods against a universe of 9 private and 1 public comparable company in the robotics sector.

Stage-progression analysis, applying a typical 1.7x multiplier to Series C funding ($129M base), implies a valuation of $219M. Peer-median analysis across 7 same-sector comparables—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D)—yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. The divergence between methods reflects stage and company-specific risk variance within the robotics universe.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $186M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median cross-method estimate of $935M. The wide range indicates material uncertainty around market comparables at GITAI's stage; Stage C businesses in this sector show significant dispersion in investor expectations. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to Series B/D cohort peers, capital efficiency trajectory, and market timing relative to robotics adoption cycles. Investors should weight stage-progression as a floor and peer-median as directional ceiling pending diligence into specific business fundamentals and competitive positioning.
